points: Q3 will test whether the Q2 demand surge was seasonal or durable: company-operated same-shop sales rose 8.3% and transactions rose 3.4% in Q2, and the print needs to show traffic stayed positive through the summer to support the long case.

The raised 2026 revenue guidance of $2.10-$2.13 billion and system same-shop sales guidance of 5%-6% mean Q3 results must keep the company on that track after a $550.9 million Q2; a miss or slowdown would call the guidance into question.

Adjusted EBITDA guidance was lifted to $385-$390 million for 2026 after Q2 EBITDA of $113.7 million; Q3 will reveal whether new shops are delivering the implied flow-through and margin expansion needed for the full-year target.

The 13-to-2 upward analyst revision skew and 90-day revenue estimate increases of 3.93% have raised the bar; Q3 needs to confirm that momentum so FY1 EPS of $0.98 and FY2 EPS of $1.31 remain achievable.
BJRI reports on October 28, just before BROS, and will provide a near-term read on restaurant traffic trends, though BROS's drive-thru beverage focus may outperform casual-dining peers.

The premium P/E versus the restaurant group is offset by a PEG near the theme median; Q3 must show the 28.6% FY1 and 34.5% FY2 EPS growth trajectory is intact to keep that valuation math working for the long.
watch: Company-operated same-shop sales growth holds at or above the Q2 8.3% pace — supports the long.
Systemwide same-shop sales growth stays within or above the raised 5%-6% full-year guidance range — supports the long.
Adjusted EBITDA progress keeps the company on track for the $385-$390 million full-year range — supports the long.
New shop openings and 2026 development pipeline remain on pace after 48 openings in Q2 — supports the long.
